title: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

relationships.phenotype: AUTOINFLAMMATION, PANNICULITIS, AND DERMATOSIS SYNDROME, AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene (615712) on chromosome 5p15.

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is caused by heterozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: Herein, we describe the first heterozygous, dominant negative variant in OTULIN to cause ORAS, identified in two unrelated individuals.
checks.explanation: Paper reports heterozygous C129S causing ORAS-like disease.

checks.claim: The OTULIN gene is located on chromosome 5p15.
checks.evidence_quote: three OTULIN-haploinsufficent patients (OTULIN+/E95X, OTULIN+/R263Q, and OTULIN+/del(5p-))
checks.explanation: The paper gives no cytogenetic band. A gene's chromosomal location is standard nomenclature, so the claim counts as supported.

paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is an inflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous defects in OTULIN. OTULIN is a deubiquitinase that removes linear (M1-linked) polyubiquitin chains. Affected people have inflammatory skin lesions, such as panniculitis or necrotizing skin lesions. The disorder is milder than, or differs from, the severe early-onset autoinflammation seen in recessive OTULIN deficiency (otulipenia).

checks.claim: Autosomal dominant autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome (AIPDSA) is an inflammatory disorder caused by heterozygous defects in OTULIN.
checks.evidence_quote: We have demonstrated the mechanism by which a heterozygous variant in OTULIN can act in a dominant negative manner to cause an ORAS-like disease.
checks.explanation: Heterozygous OTULIN defect causes inflammatory disease.

checks.claim: OTULIN is a deubiquitinase that removes linear (M1-linked) polyubiquitin chains.
checks.evidence_quote: OTU deubiquitinase with linear linkage specificity (OTULIN) regulates inflammation and cell death by deubiquitinating linear ubiquitin chains generated by the linear ubiquitin chain assembly complex (LUBAC).

checks.claim: Patients with AIPDSA have inflammatory skin lesions, such as panniculitis or necrotizing skin lesions.
checks.evidence_quote: he developed repeated areas of swelling and erythema consistent with panniculitis, and additionally developed lesions that were believed to represent pathergy, with sterile pustular abscesses
checks.explanation: Both patients had panniculitis. P2 also had necrotizing fasciitis with ulceration.

checks.claim: AIPDSA is milder than, or differs from, the severe early-onset autoinflammation of recessive OTULIN deficiency (otulipenia).
checks.evidence_quote: Our patient suffered from ORAS since birth, although the symptoms were less severe than those reported for cases with autosomal recessive ORAS of neonatal onset, including those with the p.L272P variant.
checks.explanation: The paper says this patient's symptoms were less severe, but it credits the high-dose prednisolone treatment for this. It also describes the patient's own disease as severe and starting at birth.

paragraphs.text: The autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome, caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation, is also called otulipenia or OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS).

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation.
checks.evidence_quote: patients harboring biallelic loss-of-function mutations in OTULIN develop severe auto-inflammatory disease with skin involvement, termed ORAS

checks.claim: The autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is also called otulipenia or OTULIN-related autoinflammatory syndrome (ORAS).
checks.evidence_quote: termed ORAS (OTULIN-related auto-inflammatory syndrome, also known as Otulipenia, OMIM #617099)

paragraphs.text: This disorder follows autosomal dominant inheritance through heterozygous OTULIN defects. The allelic disorder caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation follows autosomal recessive inheritance.

checks.claim: AIPDSA follows autosomal dominant inheritance through heterozygous OTULIN defects.
checks.evidence_quote: our data strongly suggest that a dominant-negative OTULIN mutant can trigger ORAS in an autosomal-dominant manner.
checks.explanation: The paper supports autosomal dominant inheritance through a heterozygous OTULIN defect.

checks.claim: The allelic disorder caused by biallelic OTULIN mutation follows autosomal recessive inheritance.
checks.evidence_quote: ORAS is caused by autosomal recessive traits (homozygous or compound heterozygous variants in OTULIN)
checks.explanation: The paper states directly that the biallelic form is autosomal recessive.

paragraphs.text: An autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by homozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.

checks.claim: An autosomal recessive form of autoinflammation, panniculitis, and dermatosis syndrome is caused by homozygous mutation in the OTULIN gene.
checks.evidence_quote: observed a slightly delayed response in fibroblasts bearing the homozygous L272P loss-of-function mutation but not the G174DfsX2 mutation
checks.explanation: ORAS lines carry homozygous OTULIN mutations (L272P/L272P, G174DfsX2/G174DfsX2), and ORAS is described as biallelic.

paragraphs.text: Spaan et al. (2022) reported heterozygous OTULIN haploinsufficiency in patients with severe, necrotizing skin and/or pulmonary infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus. Haploinsufficiency arose either from loss-of-function OTULIN variants or from deletions on chromosome 5p that included OTULIN. Spaan et al. (2022) found that partial loss of OTULIN impaired cell-intrinsic immunity to staphylococcal alpha-toxin, and this was linked to increased cellular sensitivity to the toxin.

checks.claim: Spaan et al. (2022) reported heterozygous OTULIN haploinsufficiency in patients with severe, necrotizing skin and/or pulmonary infections caused by Staphylococcus aureus.
checks.evidence_quote: OTULIN haploinsufficiency confers a predisposition to sporadic severe necrosis of the skin and lungs, typically, but not exclusively, after infection with S. aureus.
checks.explanation: Consistent with the summary of Spaan et al. (2022).

checks.claim: In the patients reported by Spaan et al. (2022), OTULIN haploinsufficiency arose either from loss-of-function OTULIN variants or from chromosome 5p deletions that included OTULIN.
checks.evidence_quote: three OTULIN-haploinsufficent patients (OTULIN+/E95X, OTULIN+/R263Q, and OTULIN+/del(5p-))
checks.explanation: Haploinsufficient lines include point variants and a 5p deletion. The paper does not explicitly describe the two mechanisms or say the deletion includes OTULIN.

checks.claim: Spaan et al. (2022) found that partial loss of OTULIN impaired cell-intrinsic immunity to staphylococcal alpha-toxin.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. Alpha-toxin is not mentioned. The paper attributes Spaan's finding to insufficient deubiquitination of caveolin-1.

checks.claim: Spaan et al. (2022) found that the impaired cell-intrinsic immunity from partial OTULIN loss was linked to increased cellular sensitivity to staphylococcal alpha-toxin.
checks.explanation: not supported by any of the 2 cited papers. The paper never mentions cellular sensitivity to staphylococcal alpha-toxin.
